headline: Google Keep gets Gemini AI to automate list creation, saving hours
summary: Gemini integration transforms Google Keep from a digital junk drawer into a productivity engine, automating list creation for everything from groceries to packing.
details: Google Keep, once a simple digital note-taking app, is now being transformed into a productivity powerhouse with the integration of Gemini AI. This feature allows users to automate the creation of lists, saving significant time and effort in daily workflows.

The 'Help me create a list' feature, powered by Gemini, has been a game-changer for users like tech analyst Parth. Instead of spending up to 20 minutes researching and formatting lists, Gemini can generate a complete, structured checklist in seconds.

To access these features, users need a Google One AI Premium plan or a supported Google Pixel device. The effectiveness of the generated lists depends on the prompt provided; detailed prompts yield incredibly accurate and useful results.

Examples of Gemini's utility include generating a week's worth of high-protein, vegetarian Mediterranean meals for two on a $100 budget, or creating a tailored packing list for a business trip, complete with tech essentials and attire recommendations.

Furthermore, by connecting the Google Workspace extension, Gemini can access and retrieve information from Google Docs, Gmail, and Keep Notes. This allows users to ask Gemini to find specific lists or information within their notes without needing to open the Keep app directly.

This integration streamlines tasks by eliminating the need for constant app switching. Users can now treat the Gemini prompt box as a command center, asking it to pull specific lists or details from their notes using simple commands like '@Google Keep get me tech essential list'.

headline: Meta's Muse AI to generate more revenue than Facebook/Instagram
summary: Mark Zuckerberg expects Meta's new personal agent to eventually surpass the company's flagship apps in revenue per user.
details: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed that the company is entering a new phase with its personal AI agent, Muse, focusing on monetization. He anticipates Muse will eventually generate more revenue per user than Meta's existing apps like Facebook and Instagram.

Despite its recent September rollout, Muse has seen significant adoption, with over 10 million users in the US and Canada. Zuckerberg stated the company aims to scale Muse to serve billions of people globally.

Operating Muse is more resource-intensive than Meta's other services. To address this, Meta plans to integrate 'commerce tools' that will charge businesses for transactions facilitated by the agent. Shopping is a primary use case, with users reportedly spending an average of $200 per purchase via Muse.

Meta will also offer AI subscriptions for heavy users, both individuals and business owners. Zuckerberg projects that revenue from Muse could eventually exceed current earnings from Meta's family of apps, citing the high average revenue per user for existing services and the potential for commerce-driven growth.

Muse is also positioned as a key component for monetizing Meta's AI glasses. While the hardware itself may not be highly profitable, integrating Muse is expected to drive sales of AI subscriptions for the glasses. Features like enhanced hearing may also be paywalled.

Muse will be available on Meta's smart glasses next month, allowing users to interact with the agent similarly to Meta AI. This integration is expected to boost subscription revenue for the hardware, though specific subscription details for the glasses remain unspecified.
